claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing tungsten particles or interconnected tungsten ligaments within a copper matrix.
The untreated W–Cu composite is prone to phase separation under service conditions.
The untreated W–Cu composite is prone to interfacial void formation under service conditions.
Tungsten particles should be coated with a thin nickel layer before composite fabrication.
A Ni interlayer promotes improved wetting between tungsten and copper.
A Ni interlayer promotes stronger interfacial bonding between tungsten and copper.
The nickel coating reduces the surface-energy mismatch between tungsten and copper.
Reducing the tungsten–copper surface-energy mismatch lowers the driving force for phase separation.
The nickel coating inhibits interfacial void formation during heat transfer and irradiation.
The improved interface facilitates more efficient thermal conduction.
A W–Cu composite made with Ni-coated tungsten particles will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise identically processed composite made with untreated tungsten particles.
Phase separation and interfacial void formation compromise the thermal conductivity of untreated W–Cu composites.
The proposed benefit applies under elevated-temperature and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between tungsten plasma-facing materials and copper cooling components.
The optimal nickel-coating thickness remains to be determined.
